summary: Council approved the fiscal 2027 budget changes, which the mayor said would eliminate planned employee furloughs and add about $800,000 for schools. Members also discussed unpaid property taxes, water and trash billing problems, and the Echo Lane sewer project. The mayor reported that former police chief Joseph Solomon pleaded guilty to 17 charges.

Mayor’s Report 
 Mayor Beauregard expressed his gratitude to the Friends of the Searles for the 
presentation and all the incredible work they have been doing.  It has been nice to see some 
more activity on the estate and seeing things come to life.   
 Mayor Beauregard addressed the Solomon situation.  As you know, last Friday, former 
Police Chief, Joseph Solomon pled guilty to all 17 charges against him, including 11 felonies.

He admitted, under oath, that he committed these crimes.  He went directly to jail and his 
taxpayer funded city pension is gone.  The city will pursue every available legal avenue to 
recover the more than one million dollars in pension benefits already paid to him.  The 
elimination of his pension under state law is also is expected to reduce Methuen’s unfunded 
pension liability by approximately 3.7 million dollars over the next twenty years.  Regardless of 
what his defenders claim on social medias, Solomon committed perjury, uttered forged police 
academy credentials, and in procurement fraud, and knowingly placed unqualified and 
improperly trained individuals into positions of public trust.  His crimes endangered public 
safety, betrayed his oath, and formed part of a broader scheme to defraud the taxpayers of 
Methuen.  But Solomon’s convictions cannot be the end of this matter.  Serious questions 
remain about whether others participated in a wider criminal conspiracy to defraud the 
Methuen taxpayers, and abused the power of city government.  Individuals were identified in 
official documents as unindicted co-conspirators.  Yet the federal investigation into Solomon 
and others was abruptly ang inexplicably closed two years ago this week without charges or any 
meaningful public explanation.  To demonstrate a unified front from Methuen leadership, he 
will be, along with Councilor Simard, bringing forward a joint resolution and an attached letter 
from the Mayor and City Council at the next meeting formally calling upon U.S. Attorney Leah 
Foley and the Department of Justice to return to Methuen, reopen the federal investigation, 
examine the evidence gathered by state and federal authorities and determine whether federal 
charges are warranted against Solomon or any else who participated in this criminal conspiracy 
to defraud our taxpayers.  Methuen has achieved an important measure of justice.  Solomon is a 
convicted felon.  He is serving time in jail and his city pension is gone.  But accountability 
cannot stop with the one person who happened to hold the title of Police Chief.  Every 
participant in this corruption, and every person who benefited from it must be investigated and 
where the evidence supports it, be fully prosecuted of federal law.

on Thursday, September 24th.  The event will begin with a club and activity fair in the cafeteria 
from 5:30 to 6:00 p.m. and from 6:00 to 8:00 p.m. families will follow their high schoolers

Policies sub-committees will meet this week and Gina Bozek from the school district will

Regarding paving, I am sure you noticed they are extremely ambitious.  Road 
improvement initiative is well underway.  We have been making some great progress in the 
push to fix our roads.  We tackled Forest Street and we are working on Milk Street now.  We 
will be fixing badly deteriorated sections of Pleasant Street, Jackson Street, and Pleasant Valley 
Street soon on top of the residential side streets that need attention.  He’s been working with 
Chair Soto on drafting a Home Rule Petition being modeled after a  2014 special act for the 
Town of Barnstable that would give the City Council the ability to vote to pave, but not 
formally accept certain unaccepted ways that have been open to use by the general public for at 
least twenty consecutive years and connect to other accepted ways.  He hears the frustrations 
from the residents who live on these streets and thinks the Barnstable model is one way we 
might be able to help them. 
Regarding the dangerous intersections at Park and Lawrence Streets in the east Milton 
and Prospect streets.  Preliminary designs are now in place for both intersections.  DPW is 
meeting weekly with TECH and he is invited certain residents who live near these intersections 
to join us in an upcoming meeting with TECH so we can make sure their concerns are heard 
before plans are finalized.   
Regarding trash and recycling, he expects to present a new trash and recycling contract 
to the City Council for consideration and approval this Fall. This will mark the culmination of 
what he has been calling our “trash reset”, including bringing on the city’s first Sanitation 
Coordinator, Karina, in strengthening oversight of this essential service.  Our goal is to have 
more reliable collection, clear communication, and greater accountability when problems arise.  
The proposed contract in its financial service implications will be presented as part of the City 
Council’s review.   
He mentioned that we heard tonight about weights and measures from Mr. Jones and 
this is a topic that we were thinking about possibly bringing to this meeting but we’ll probably 
do it at the next meeting where we have an amendment to the wage and salary grid so that we 
can formally bring that position back into existence.  It has not been a thing since, as was 
mentioned, roughly 2020, with the retirement of the inspector, John Gibney.  He has been in 
touch with the state about this.  That is something that is moving.   
On tonight’s agenda we have the second read for his request for a one-year moratorium 
to give Methuen time to assess the potential impacts of data center development and establish 
appropriate local regulations.  His central concerns are affordability, utility capacity, and water 
use.  Large data centers can require a substantial electricity and cooling resources, and we need 
to understand how a proposed facility would affect our infrastructure and whether any 
associated costs could fall on residents and existing businesses.  At the last meeting, the 
amendment to the table of uses was removed from the zoning ordinance for the moratorium to

If we were to pass the temporary moratorium during the moratorium period, we would work 
toward enforceable standards addressing electricity supply, water demand, cooling systems,

from the Massachusetts Department of Energy Resources, and we have submitted 
documentation to DPU for approval.  We are working with our municipal electricity 
aggregation consultant, Colonial Power Group, to bring additional electricity savings to income 
eligible households participating in our Methuen Community Choice Power Supply program.  
The current projection is a discount of approximately 2.2 cents per kilowatt hour, reducing the 
program standard electric supply rate for eligible participants from 12.8 $0.03 to approximately 
10.6 $0.02per kilowatt hour.  Our goal is to begin delivering these savings in early 2027, subject 
to the remaining approvals and implementation requirements.  We will share as the process 
moves forward.   
The city’s transition to the Group Insurance Commission remains scheduled for January 
1st, 2027.  As we have discussed, this is a major structural reform intended to provide more 
predictable costs and address the recurring deficits associate with the city’s health insurance trust 
fund.  The special enrollment period will run from October 5th to October 30th.  Anyone wishing 
to have GIC coverage January 1st, must apply during that period.  Enrollment is not automatic. 
Participants should review their plan options, confirm with their doctors and hospitals in

required government issued marriage and birth certificates now to avoid delays or rejected 
applications.  This is something that the state requires regarding GIC enrollment.  Folks need 
marriage and birth certificate for any dependents.  He is decided to make those available to city 
employees with a waived fee so that we are not charging our employees to get their hands on 
those for the sake of the transition.  The city has scheduled in person and virtual information

December.  Any questions that individuals have, can be directed to the Employee Benefits office

are many retirees out there, so we are reiterating this.
